newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says Italy no longer "ugly duckling"-ANSA.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says Italy no longer "ugly duckling"-ANSA.

text.p: Italy is no longer the "ugly duckling" of Europe after Bonn said it would go ahead with plans to revalue gold reserves in the face of Bundesbank opposition, news agency ANSA quoted the Treasury minister as saying.
The news agency said Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told leaders of parliamentary parties allied to the government "we are no longer the ugly duckling of Europe" at a meeting this morning.

Ciampi is spearheading government efforts to sort out public finances in time for the planned launch of a single European currency in 1999. Italy's track record for fiscal rectitude has often been compared unfavourably with that of its North European neighbours led by Germany.

A plan by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel to revalue gold reserves to help cut Germany's budget deficit has been rejected by the Bundesbank which said it could undermine the single European currency from the outset. --Rome newsroom +396-6782505
